text:
Cara: heads-up — noticed a big span backlog in inference-prod overnight, looks correlated with heavy tenant fanout to the otlp exporter. memory on a few nodes spiked. :eyes:
Miguel: hmm. is that the per-tenant fanout we added last month? I thought the shim bounded queues would prevent unbounded growth.
Priya: we added per-tenant routing but the backing queue was left unbounded in python service due to legacy wrapper. could be leaking during retries.
Tom: language gap here — python sdk uses background thread + queue, go has buffered channel, rust is using crossbeam but some paths call `flush()` synchronously which can backpressure callers. different behaviors under load.
Miguel: proposal: add per-tenant bounded buffer + tenant-level throttle + a drop policy (oldest/none) and emit a lightweight metric when we drop spans so billing/alerts keep fidelity. config sketch: 
```
otel:
  exporter:
    type: otlp
    per_tenant:
      buffer_size: 2000
      drop_policy: oldest
      throttle: 50/sec
```
Cara: that config looks sane. we also saw memory blowups when a node lost network to collector; rust process built up 100k queued spans before OOM. need a hard cap.
Priya: agree on hard cap. also we should sample earlier — head-based sampling so low-value internal spans never enter the queue. saves cycles.
Tom: caution: some infra wants every request-span for billing/chargeback. if we drop, we must still emit counters: `spans_ingested`, `spans_dropped_reason=buffer_full` per tenant. metrics are single-line and cheap.
infra-bot: ALERT: exporter_queue_size(node-12) = 92% (span_queue=1840/2000) — action required
Miguel: rollout plan: implement in sdk-shim, enable per-service feature-flag. canary 5% tenants for 30m and watch `span_drop_rate`, `export_latency_p50/p95`, and node memory. auto rollback on >0.5% span drop or memory > 85%.
Cara: for cross-lang API, let's standardize a `span.drop_reason` enum attr and `otel.exporter.routing.tenant_id` resource attr so downstream dedup/metrics can correlate. would also make logs/console dashboards easier.
Priya: I'll draft a short RFC + config schema and a minimal python/go shim PR. Tom — can you sketch the rust wrapper behavior (bounded channel + atomic counters) so we align semantics?
Tom: yep I'll put a prototype in my branch tonight. we should also decide whether the exporter handoff is async-with-backpressure or sync-fails-fast for critical paths. i'd prefer async+bounded.
Priya: cool. i'll include tests for OOM/regression and a dashboard plan (per-tenant span ingestion, drop_rate, exporter_backpressure).
Cara: thanks — prioritize prototype + canary toggles. ping me when drafts are up :thumbsup:
